newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia inflation rate falls to two-year low.
newsitem.headline: Australia inflation rate falls to two-year low.

text.p: Australia's annual inflation rate fell to a two-year low of 2.1 percent in the three months to September, the Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday.
The figure, slightly below analysts' forecasts of around 2.2 percent, boosted chances for an early cut in interest rates, said economists.

But economists said the Reserve Bank of Australia would examine key wages data on Thursday before considering any cut in the 7.0 percent official rate. The bank warned last week that pay agreements were currently running too high.
"I still think the odds of a rate cut before Christmas are a touch better than 50-50." said Saul Eslake, chief economist at the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ).
The Bureau of Statistics said the consumer price index rose 0.3 percent in the September quarter for an annual inflation rate of 2.1 percent, down from 3.1 percent in the June quarter.
Underlying inflation, seen as the better guide to future monetary policy, rose 0.5 percent in the quarter to stand at 2.4 percent for the year, just below market expectations.
